task.title: Ask deploy bundle probe
task.problem: Production chunks linked from / contain no api/ask string, so the Ask console never calls the model tier, and nothing in the repo detects a stale deploy. A read-only bundle check is the fastest way to tell a stale deploy from a missing call.
non_goals: changing the ask route, the console or lib/ask-tier.ts
running the probe against https://otohime.dev as a verification item
action_items: Create lib/ask-deploy.ts exporting chunkCarriesAskCall(text: string): boolean and bundleCarriesAskCall(chunks: string[]): boolean. The match is the literal path api/ask and nothing looser.

Add lib/ask-deploy.test.ts with cases: a chunk containing /api/ask returns true, a chunk without it returns false, an empty bundle returns false, and a chunk containing api/ask-old does not count as the console call.

Add scripts/probe-ask-deploy.mjs: fetch BASE_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:3000), collect /_next/static/chunks/*.js links from the HTML, fetch each chunk, print the count of chunks checked and the count carrying the call, exit 0 only when bundleCarriesAskCall is true.
Add scripts/probe-ask-deploy.sh as a thin wrapper that runs the .mjs with node and passes BASE_URL through. Do not change app/, components/ or the route.
Do not set env, redeploy or touch Vercel. This task only adds the probe and its unit tests.
task.acceptance_criteria: A pure function reports whether a set of built JS chunks carries the console's api/ask call, and scripts/probe-ask-deploy.sh applies it to BASE_URL: it exits 0 when a chunk linked from / carries the call and 1 otherwise; npm test passes.

entries.summary: slowness verdict fix_plan by run-8771: pm-255 is held by an orphaned after_plan edge, not by its own work. It was split out of pm-248 at 04:28:31 (dec-55726, reason max_plan_elapsed) with after_plan_id=pm-248, and t-1557 inherited started_at=04:27:53 from its approval under pm-248, so the task_duration clock has only ever measured queue… · fix plan pm-260

evidence.idea:
Release split parts whose after_plan parent is abandoned (plan-manager, mono-v2).

What is broken: when a plan is split for max_plan_elapsed, the follow-on part gets after_plan_id = parent and waits until the parent is done. If the parent is then abandoned, the orchestrator records only an advisory decision line after_plan_orphaned ("stay held until you reject them or reopen the parent"), raises no escalation or operator_action, and the part sits in queued forever with progress waiting/after_plan. The decider that abandons the parent is not told this: run-8680's abandon note for pm-248 says "Abandoning frees pm-255 to run", which is false. The slowness watchdog then fires task_duration on the part's first task because the task's started_at was stamped at its approval under the parent, so it counts time in which the part never held a slot; after the one allowed pause the hold becomes invisible.

Evidence: pm-255 (part of pm-248) created 2026-10-26T04:28:31 with after_plan_id=pm-248; pm-248 abandoned 04:49:13 (dec-55807, acceptance_exhausted) with dec-55806 after_plan_orphaned advisory=true naming pm-255; dec-55931 promotion_skipped at 05:12:21 reason after_plan; explain_schedule at 08:15 progress.state=waiting reason=after_plan holders=[pm-248], execution_started_at=null, slots free 2 of 4; esc-389 slow_plan task_duration 3h46m22s on t-1557 with 0 SWE attempts, 0 runs, 0 CI jobs; investigator run-8771 verdict fix_plan.

What done looks like: (1) When a plan with waiting parts is abandoned, the orchestrator either clears the parts' after_plan hold (they re-enter the promotion line in their own right; the parent's abandon decision note is attached to each part's timeline) or raises a blocking operator_action per part with the choice release / reject, with a ready_probe on the part's progress.state leaving after_plan; the advisory-only after_plan_orphaned line is no longer the sole signal. The decider prompt and the abandon decision text name the real effect on parts. (2) A unit test covers: parent abandoned with one part held -> part released (or operator_action raised) within one tick; parent done -> part released as today; parent reopened -> hold restored. (3) Slowness task_duration measures from the task's first ready transition inside a plan that has started executing (execution_started_at set), or the breach names the after_plan hold as its cause, so a part queued behind a parent is not flagged as a slow task with zero attempts; a unit test covers a part with execution_started_at=null past slow_task_duration. (4) As the immediate board effect, pm-255 is released from after_plan pm-248 and reaches queued/startable, so t-1557 (Ask deploy bundle probe) is dispatched to a software_engineer; if the code fix cannot land first, an operator releases pm-255 (reopen pm-248 then re-abandon after the parts are promoted, or clear the after_plan edge) and that release is recorded on pm-255's timeline.
evidence.cause: pm-255 is held by an orphaned after_plan edge, not by its own work. It was split out of pm-248 at 04:28:31 (dec-55726, reason max_plan_elapsed) with after_plan_id=pm-248, and t-1557 inherited started_at=04:27:53 from its approval under pm-248, so the task_duration clock has only ever measured queue time: pm-255 has execution_started_at=null, run_count=1 (this investigator), t-1557 has 0 SWE attempts and 0 fix cycles, and no run, CI job or pipeline for it exists. The parent pm-248 was abandoned at 04:49:13 by decider run-8680 (dec-55807, acceptance_exhausted); its rationale states explicitly "Abandoning frees pm-255 to run", but the orchestrator recorded the opposite in the same instant (dec-55806 after_plan_orphaned, advisory=true): "pm-248 is abandoned and 1 plan part(s) wait for it: pm-255. They stay held (no research, no promotion) until you reject them or reopen pm-248." Nobody acted on that advisory line; at 05:12:21 promotion_skipped (dec-55931) still named after_plan held by pm-248, and explain_schedule at 08:15 shows progress waiting/after_plan with holder pm-248, never_parks=true and an empty promotion line, while slots are 2 of 4 free (otohime uses 1) and max_active_fix_plans=1 with fix_used=0. The task contract itself is narrow (four new files, qa=skip, local npm test/typecheck gates), so edit_task and split would change nothing, and a plain resume returns the plan to queued behind the same abandoned parent, where the watchdog (which pauses once per spell) would no longer catch it. The platform needs a fix first: a split part whose parent is abandoned must be released or must raise a real operator_action, and the decider must not be told that abandoning frees it when it does not. No open or planned platform issue (16 open, 26 planned, all read) covers this.

entries.reason:
# Change request: Ask the Ink must reach the model tier on production

For the product owner. Seasons and the torn-sheet 404 pass live at 1366x768 and 390x844 (acceptance_report_1). The Ask bit does not work for a visitor on https://otohime.dev.

## What a visitor still cannot do
- Ask a question and get an answer generated from Work, Projects and Notes. The console answers only with the offline canned text.
- See the console call the model tier. Production gets no GET /api/ask and no POST /api/ask from the console.

## Evidence
- GET and POST https://otohime.dev/api/ask: HTTP 404.
- scripts/probe-ask.sh with BASE_URL=https://otohime.dev: 63 ok, 23 failed. Failures are the model-tier checks and the tier-off GET check.
- 17 /_next/static chunks linked from /: none contains api/ask. Main has the call (components/ask-console.tsx, lib/ask-tier.ts) since 8e02b8d. The deployed build predates 8e02b8d, or that code did not ship.

## Which service
The Ask console (components/ask-console.tsx, lib/ask-tier.ts) and its route app/api/ask/route.ts, served on https://otohime.dev (Vercel).

## Requested outcome
1. Production runs a web build at or after 8e02b8d. The chunks linked from / contain api/ask, and the console sends one GET /api/ask on open.
2. The model tier is on in production: GET /api/ask returns 200 with "enabled":true. This is operator action set-env:ask-llm-production (esc-381): a person with the Vercel account sets ASK_LLM=1 and a server-only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, then redeploys.
3. A visitor's question on https://otohime.dev sends one POST /api/ask, and the model's lines and cited pages print. If the model tier is unavailable, the console still shows the canned answer with no visible error.

Acceptance walks production again once 1 to 3 hold, at both widths.

entries.summary:
otohime.dev — three new bits for the paper-and-ink pocket console:

1) "Ask the Ink" — a small AI oracle on the site that answers visitors' questions about my data-engineering work, projects and notes. Answers are grounded only in the site's own content (Work, Projects, Notes), stream in as hand-inked typewriter text inside a pocket-console screen, and cite which page they came from. Rate-limited, cheap model, graceful offline fallback with canned answers. Inspiration: an AI-driven personal site with an agent that answers questions about the owner's work history — https://x.com/agentcommunity_/status/2114118498901164504

2) Paper almanac seasons — the paper, ink tints and a light ambient layer (ink-drawn petals, falling leaves, rain streaks, snow specks via SVG filters) follow the visitor's real season and hemisphere, with a tiny season dial to switch manually. Respect prefers-reduced-motion. Inspiration: a personal site whose interactive background follows your season with a season selector — https://x.com/bepituLaz/status/2107128873519583570

3) A playful 404 "lost page" — the missing page is a torn, crumpled sheet; visitors can smooth it out / play a tiny ink mini-game to find their way back, with links to the main pages. Inspiration: a fun 404 easter egg on a personal site — https://x.com/graiz/status/2113253832150904880 ; and drawable, poppable shader bubbles on a portfolio homepage — https://x.com/codrops/status/2107403538791813539
